title: Khrushchev Lied
author: Grover Furr
desc: Análisis documental que cuestiona las acusaciones del Informe Secreto de Jrushchov contra Stalin.
tesis: Furr analiza las 61 acusaciones específicas del Informe Secreto de Jrushchov (1956) contra Stalin y argumenta, con documentación de archivos soviéticos desclasificados, que la mayoría son falsas o distorsionadas. No es una defensa de Stalin sino una deconstrucción documental del texto que creó la 'leyenda negra'. El Informe Secreto fue un acto político de Jrushchov para legitimar su propio poder, no un acto de verdad histórica.
ideas: El Informe Secreto de Jrushchov fue un acto político para legitimar el nuevo liderazgo, no un ejercicio de verdad histórica.
Furr usa archivos soviéticos desclasificados para cuestionar las acusaciones específicas — es análisis documental, no propaganda.
La 'leyenda negra' de Stalin se construyó sobre un documento que nunca fue verificado críticamente.
contexto: Obra revisionista basada en archivos soviéticos desclasificados. La metodología de Furr ha sido criticada por selectiva, pero su contribución es demostrar que el Informe Secreto de Jrushchov nunca fue verificado críticamente por la academia occidental.

conexiones.razon: Losurdo contextualiza históricamente; Furr cuestiona las fuentes documentales del Informe Secreto.
La Historia del PCUS es la versión oficial estalinista; Furr cuestiona la versión oficial antiestalinista.

tl: Lenin dicta su supuesto Testamento

The document in question was not widely known in the party history as Lenin's 'Testament'. Khrushchev took this term from Trotsky, who wrote a book with that title in 1934. It had never been known as such except among oppositionists.
El 13.º Congreso confirma a Stalin como Secretario General

This document of Lenin's was made known to the delegates at the 13th Party Congress who discussed the question of transferring Stalin from the position of Secretary General. The delegates declared themselves in favor of retaining Stalin in this post.
Asesinato de Serguéi Kirov en Leningrado, detonante de la Gran Purga

As Arch Getty has pointed out, several Soviet and post-Soviet commissions tried to find evidence that Stalin was involved in Kirov's assassination, and all failed. Sudoplatov too concluded there was no reason to suspect Stalin in this assassination.
Primer Proceso de Moscú contra Zinóviev y Kámenev

Sentencing Zinoviev and Kamenev, among others, to be shot for treason was not arbitrary if they were guilty, as all the evidence at our disposal at present suggests. Therefore, we have every reason to conclude that Khrushchev lied hypocritically.
Ejecución del mariscal Tujachevski y la trama militar

In his recently-published confession-interrogation of April 26 1939 Ezhov fully confirms the existence of three separate, competing military conspiracies. Even that documentation demonstrates their guilt beyond any reasonable doubt.
Yezhovshchina, represión masiva del NKVD

The interrogations of Ezhov and Frinovskii published in early 2006 fully confirm Ezhov's deliberate torturing and killing of a great many innocent people. He organized these atrocities to cover up his own involvement in the Rightist conspiracy.
Tercer Proceso de Moscú: Bujarin, Rykov y los médicos

At the March 1938 Moscow Trial of Bukharin, Rykov and others two medical doctors, Pletnev and Levin, had confessed to a conspiracy to bring about the deaths of the writer Maxim Gorkii, Valerian V. Kuibyshev, a Politburo member.
Ejecución de Yezhov y sus subordinados

Nikolaev-Zhurid was finally arrested in October 1939 under Beria. Nikolaev-Zhurid was also executed, and therefore probably tried, at the same time as were Ezhov and Eikhe, in early February 1940. So was Ushakov.
Invasión alemana del 22 de junio y reacción de Stalin

Georgi Dimitrov, the Bulgarian head of the Comintern, wrote in his diary that he was summoned to the Kremlin at 7 a.m. on June 22 1941. He remarked: Striking calmness, resoluteness, confidence of Stalin and all the others.
Desastre de Járkov atribuido falsamente a Stalin

Marshal Vasilevskii directly called Khrushchev's version of the Khar'kov defense a lie. He says that Khrushchev and General Kirponos were in fact given plans and sample rocket-launchers, as well as advice on how to build their own weapons.
Deportaciones de pueblos del Cáucaso y Crimea
In 1939 there were 218,000 Crimean Tartars. By 1944 20,000 Crimean Tartar soldiers had joined the Nazi forces and were fighting against the Red Army. So the charge of massive collaboration sticks.
Caso de Leningrado y rivalidades sucesorias
The Leningrad Affair is mysterious, important, and fascinating. There is plenty of reason to think that it was not simply a question of falsification but that serious crimes were involved.
Caso de los Médicos abierto por el MGB
The Doctors' Plot was taken up by the MGB in 1952. Timashuk's letters were written in 1948. They concerned Zhdanov's treatment in his final illness. They mentioned no Jewish doctors at all.
Muerte de Stalin y golpe interno de Khrushchev

On March 5 1953, with Stalin not yet dead, the old Politburo members met and abolished the enlarged Presidium which had been approved at the 19th Party Congress the previous October. This was virtually a coup d'etat within the Party.
Detención y ejecución de Beria

Khrushchev and the others had Lavrentii Beria arrested suddenly on June 26, 1953 on false charges and without any evidence. Subsequently they had Beria killed, together with six others who had been close associates of his.
XX Congreso del PCUS sacude al PCM

Not one specific statement of 'revelation' that Khrushchev made about either Stalin or Beria turned out to be true. Among those that can be checked for verification, every single one turns out to be false.
Trotsky rehabilitado de hecho por el Discurso Secreto

That the 'Secret Speech' constituted an unacknowledged 'rehabilitation' of Trotsky was recognized by Trotsky's widow Sedova who, within a day of the Speech, applied to the Presidium of the 20th Party Congress for full rehabilitation.
Khrushchev purga a Malenkov, Mólotov y Kaganóvich

In July 1957 Khrushchev called a CC Plenum to have Malenkov, Molotov, Kaganovich, and Shepilov removed from the leadership simply because they disagreed with his policies and had tried to get Khrushchev voted out of the Party leadership.
